subject: SDK road-test & local sample kit — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romano <alex.romano@brightpath.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SDK road-test & local sample kit — next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps to get your engineers ramped locally so you can validate latency, auth, and structured-output/tool-calling patterns we discussed.

Recap (short):
- PoC goal: integrate Redwood inference for chat + tool-calling and compare embeddings + reranker for search reranking.
- Preferred runtime: your team signaled TypeScript-first, but we will provide both TS + Python quickstarts.
- Security: you need SSO + regional routing (US) and audit logs.

Proposed immediate deliverables:
1) Lightweight sample kit (TS + Python) that runs locally (Docker) with env var toggles for auth, region, and model variant. — attached as brightpath-sample-apps.zip
2) A one-page local quickstart (local-quickstart.md) showing: Docker compose, env, sample requests for function-calling and structured JSON output, and a sample reranker pipeline.
3) A 60-minute technical walkthrough (engineer-to-engineer) to step through local run, OAuth/SSO binding, and routing rules.

Asks from your side:
- Confirm preferred date/time for a technical sync (we suggested Tue 6/27 below).
- Provide a test service account or let us create a scoped API key for BrightPath (read-only logging + limited ttl) so we can preseed the sample with a realistic key.
- Any must-have compliance constraints we should bake into the quickstart (data retention window, no external logging, etc.).

Attachments: brightpath-sample-apps.zip (zip of example TS + Python apps), local-quickstart.md (single-page run instructions).

If this looks good Ill have Camila produce the minimal TS sample that demonstrates function-calling + structured output and include a simple reranker recipe.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Romano <alex.romano@brightpath.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Gil <maria.gil@brightpath.com>, security@brightpath.com
Date: 2028-06-25T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK road-test & local sample kit — next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before the walk-through: 

1) Language preference: our frontend team wants TypeScript first (Node 18) and then Python for backend scoring — TS as primary is fine.
2) Local environment: they need a Docker-first flow (we don't want to install global SDKs on dev machines); can the samples be run with docker-compose up and expose a local /invoke endpoint?
3) Auth: we require SSO integration (OIDC) for internal developers. Can the sample demonstrate exchange of an OIDC token for a short-lived Redwood credential or show how to wire our IdP?
4) Data residency: all logs for the PoC must stay in the US region and we need a short note on what the SDK transmits by default (no PII).

We're available Tue 6/27 at 10:00 AM PT for the walkthrough — can you confirm? Also looping Maria (CTO) and security so they can decide whether to share a test account.

On the attachments: I didn't get the zip in the demo session; could Camila attach the TS readme and a minimal docker-compose example in the thread?

Thanks,
Alex Romano
Sr. Staff Software Engineer, BrightPath
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romano <alex.romano@brightpath.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-25T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK road-test & local sample kit — next steps

Alex — appreciate the specifics. Quick answers and what well ship by EOD: 

- TS primary: yes. The sample kit will include a Node 18 TypeScript app that exposes /invoke behind a local express server and a docker-compose.yml to run everything locally. The compose file mounts a .env file for API key / OIDC token config so devs can run without installing the SDK globally.

- Docker flow: docker-compose up starts two services: sample-app (TS) and a local proxy that simulates our routing rules (you can toggle region: US/EU via env). We'll include a make target `make local-run` in the readme.

- Auth/SSO: we will include a short pattern showing how to exchange an OIDC id_token from your IdP for a short-lived Redwood session token via an OAuth exchange endpoint. Note: this is a sample pattern — for production we recommend using your IdP to mint constrained service credentials via our admin APIs. We'll provide a small script (exchange_oidc.sh) and a sample .env.example.

- Structured output & function-calling: the TS sample demonstrates calling a model with a function schema and validating structured JSON output on the client. We'll also include a minimal mocked tool process (a webhook-style handler) so you can test end-to-end locally.

- Embeddings + reranker: included as a separate sample flow (scripts/embeddings_rerank.ts) that shows creating embeddings, indexing them into a local vector store (sqlite + faiss/annoy shim) and then running a small re-ranking step. It's intentionally lightweight so it runs on a developer laptop.

We'll attach ts-sample-readme.md (contains the docker-compose snippet, env vars, and quick run commands) and push the samples to the GitHub repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/brightpath-samples (branch: jb/brightpath-quickstart).

Proposed next steps:
- Tech walkthrough: Tue 2028-06-27 10:00 AM PT — confirm and we'll send a calendar invite with dial-in + agenda (1hr: 20m local run + 25m auth/routing + 15m Q&A).
- Provide a temporary scoped API key or allow us to create a test service account with the necessary scopes (we'll request logs-only access for debugging).

Attachments: ts-sample-readme.md (included below).

--
Attached: ts-sample-readme.md

# TS Sample README (excerpt)
Prereqs: docker, docker-compose, Node 18 (optional if you run via container)
Quick run: cp .env.example .env && docker-compose up --build
Services:
- sample-app: Node/Express + Redwood SDK wrapper
- proxy: local routing proxy to simulate region selection
Env vars of interest:
- REDWOOD_API_KEY (or use OIDC_EXCHANGE_URL + OIDC_ID_TOKEN)
- REDWOOD_REGION (us / eu)
Sample endpoints:
- POST /invoke  --> forwards to Redwood with function schema in body
- POST /rerank  --> runs embedding + rerank script

Note: we include a small script exchange_oidc.sh that shows how to call our token exchange endpoint; swap the URL and client_id for your IdP.

Thanks for the fast turnaround. See you Tuesday.

— Alex
